blocks.title: Characteristics of living things
blocks.md: Living things carry out seven life processes (**MRS GREN**): **m**ovement, **r**espiration (release of energy from food), **s**ensitivity (responding to changes), **g**rowth, **r**eproduction, **e**xcretion (removing waste) and **n**utrition (taking in food). Non-living things such as stones and cars do not do all of these.

blocks.caption: Groups of animals with an example from Cameroon.
blocks.alt: Six boxes: fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, mammals and invertebrates, each with a key feature and an example.

blocks.title: Plants and animals
blocks.md:
**Plants** make their own food by photosynthesis, have cell walls and usually do not move from place to place. **Animals** eat other living things, have no cell walls and usually move about.

Animals with a **backbone** are **vertebrates**; those without are **invertebrates** (insects, worms, snails, spiders).

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- A bat is a mammal, not a bird: it has fur and feeds its young with milk.
- A whale lives in water but is a mammal.
- Plants are alive: they grow, reproduce and respond to light.

blocks.title: Classify the animal
blocks.statement: An animal has dry scaly skin, a backbone and lays eggs on land. Which group is it?
steps: Dry scaly skin and eggs laid on land fit the reptiles.
blocks.answer: A reptile (for example a lizard or python).

blocks.title: Is it alive?
blocks.statement: A seed does not seem to move or grow. Is it alive? Give a reason.
steps: A dormant seed respires very slowly.
When given water, air and warmth it germinates and grows.
blocks.answer: Yes: it respires and can grow into a plant.

objectives: State that living things are made of cells.

blocks.title: The cell
blocks.md:
The **cell** is the basic unit of all living things. Most cells are too small to see without a **microscope**. Parts of a cell:

- **Cell membrane**: controls what enters and leaves.
- **Cytoplasm**: jelly where reactions happen.
- **Nucleus**: controls the cell.

**Plant cells** also have a **cell wall** (support), **chloroplasts** (photosynthesis) and a large **vacuole** (cell sap).

blocks.caption: A plant cell and an animal cell.
blocks.alt: A rectangular plant cell labelled cell wall, nucleus, vacuole and chloroplast beside a round animal cell with only a nucleus labelled.

blocks.title: Magnification
blocks.md:
**Magnification = size of the image ÷ actual size** (both in the same unit).

For a microscope: **total magnification = eyepiece × objective**. Example: ×10 eyepiece and ×40 objective give ×400.

Specialised cells: **red blood cells** carry oxygen; **root hair cells** absorb water; **nerve cells** carry messages.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- The cell wall (plants only, rigid) is not the cell membrane (all cells, thin).
- Animal cells do not have chloroplasts.
- A cell drawing must show the size: write the magnification beside it.

blocks.title: Magnification of a drawing
blocks.statement: A cell is drawn 30 mm wide. Its actual width is 0.3 mm. Find the magnification.

blocks.title: Total magnification
blocks.statement: Eyepiece ×10 and objective ×40. Find the total magnification.

objectives: Name the parts of a flowering plant and their functions.
Write the word equation for photosynthesis.
State the conditions needed for germination.
reviewNotes: Cassava tuber described as a swollen root (standard); check local textbook wording.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Parts of a plant and their jobs
blocks.md:
- **Roots**: hold the plant and absorb water and mineral salts.
- **Stem**: supports the leaves and carries water and food.
- **Leaves**: make food by photosynthesis.
- **Flower**: reproduction; after fertilisation it forms the **fruit** with **seeds**.

blocks.caption: A flowering plant.
blocks.alt: A plant drawing with the flower, leaf, stem and roots labelled.

blocks.title: Photosynthesis
blocks.md:
Green plants make food (glucose) in their leaves using **light** absorbed by **chlorophyll**:

**carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen**

Carbon dioxide enters the leaf through tiny holes called **stomata**. Water comes from the roots. The glucose is used for energy and stored as **starch**.

blocks.title: Germination
blocks.md: A seed **germinates** when it has **water**, **air (oxygen)** and **warmth**. It does not need light. To test one factor, set up tubes that differ in only that factor: dry seeds (no water), seeds under oil-covered boiled water (no air), seeds in a refrigerator (cold), and a control with all three.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Plants do not eat soil: they make food from carbon dioxide and water.
- Seeds need oxygen (air) to germinate, not light.
- The dry-seed tube lacks only water: keep every other condition the same.

blocks.title: Interpret a germination experiment
blocks.statement: Four tubes hold bean seeds. Tube A is dry, B is moist and warm, C is moist but in a refrigerator, D is under a layer of oil on boiled water. Only B germinates. What do the results show?
steps: A fails: water is needed. C fails: warmth is needed.
D fails: air (oxygen) is needed. B has all three and germinates.
blocks.answer: Water, warmth and air are needed for germination.

blocks.title: Which part?
blocks.statement: Cassava stems are cut and planted and grow into new plants. Cassava tubers store starch. Which plant part is the tuber and what does it store?
steps: Cassava tubers grow underground and are swollen roots.
They store starch made in the leaves.
